newsitem.title: MEXICO: Petrochemicals key to privatization plan - Zedillo.
newsitem.headline: Petrochemicals key to privatization plan - Zedillo.

text.p: The controversial plan to privatize a petrochemical unit of the state oil monopoly Pemex is a "focal point" for Mexico's entire plan to privatize state enterprises, Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo said.

"It has turned into a focal point for the success or failure of the policies of privatization," Zedillo said in an interview with the Spanish-language news network Telenoticias, according to a report published Sunday in the newspaper La Jornada.
The proposed sale of one of two petrochemical units has divided Zedillo's Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) and Mexican politicians in general, invoking nationalist passions and legal concerns.
Opponents of the sale claim it would violate the Mexican constitution, which decrees that petroleum production must remain in the hands of the state.
Zedillo said the legal questions were still being studied by the executive branch.
"Once the legality of it is cleared up, we'll go to work on the political issues," Zedillo said.
Meanwhile, Zedillo praised the progress of privatizations in other fields such as telecommuncations, airports, sea ports, railroads and natural gas distribution.

"All of the privatizations that were started during my government are marching forward successfully and, certainly, all of them have implied legal changes, including constitutional ones, that were fully supported by my party," Zedillo said.
